section: Approaches and initiatives in AP industry - industrial policy, single desk, MSMEs, industrial nodes
subsections: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: The current flagship policy of Andhra Pradesh for Sub-Large, Large, Mega and Ultra Mega units is:
accepted.x: Industrial Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29 is the current flagship policy for Sub-Large, Large, Mega and Ultra Mega units.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact policy by matching its coverage and period.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the validity of the Industrial Development Policy (4.0):
1. It is valid for five years from the date of notification.
2. Its policy period is 2024-29.
3. It was notified on 12 December 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The policy is valid for five years, covers 2024-29, and was notified on 26 October 2024, not 12 December 2024.
accepted.tq: Separate the common policy period from the incorrect notification date.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Policy)
 a. Single Desk Policy
 b. MSME Policy
 c. Industrial Development Policy
 d. Industrial Development Policy (4.0)

List-II (Period)
 i. 2024-29
 ii. 2015-20
 iii. 2020-23
 iv. 2023-27

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: The Single Desk Policy and MSME Policy belong to 2015-20; the IDP editions cover 2020-23, 2023-27 and 2024-29 respectively.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with incorrect policy periods.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT stated as a target of the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy 2023-27?
o: A target relating to industrial development during 2023-27
Both a 25% industry share in GSDP and end-to-end facilitation in two weeks
accepted.x: The statements regarding a 25% industry share in GSDP and end-to-end facilitation in two weeks were not stated targets of IDP 2023-27.
accepted.tq: Find the option containing the two specifically rejected target claims.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct target for manufacturing Gross Value Added under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29?
o: Increase from ₹30 lakh crore in FY24 to ₹7.3 lakh crore
Increase from ₹3.4 lakh crore in FY24 to ₹7.3 lakh crore
Increase from ₹7.3 lakh crore in FY24 to ₹3.4 lakh crore
Increase from ₹3.4 lakh crore in FY24 to ₹30 lakh crore
accepted.x: The policy targets an increase in manufacturing GVA from ₹3.4 lakh crore in FY24 to ₹7.3 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Match the base figure with the intended target figure and direction of change.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents three major targets of Industrial Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29?
o: Investment ₹10 lakh crore, FDI US$30 billion and three lakh manufacturing jobs
Investment ₹7.3 lakh crore, FDI US$20 billion and five lakh manufacturing jobs
Investment ₹30 lakh crore, FDI US$5 billion and ten lakh manufacturing jobs
Investment ₹30 lakh crore, FDI US$10 billion and five lakh manufacturing jobs
accepted.x: The policy targets ₹30 lakh crore investment, US$10 billion FDI and five lakh manufacturing jobs.
accepted.tq: Check whether the figures belong to investment, FDI and employment in the correct order.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: The target for industrial parks and exports under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29 is:
o: 200 industrial parks and increase exports from US$10 billion to US$30 billion
40+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$20 billion to US$175 billion
175+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$20 billion to US$40 billion
175+ industrial parks and increase exports from US$40 billion to US$20 billion
accepted.x: The policy targets more than 175 industrial parks and an increase in exports from US$20 billion to US$40 billion.
accepted.tq: Pair the infrastructure target with the correct export base and destination figures.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: The motto of the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Development Policy (4.0) is to:
o: Increase imports and restrict domestic manufacturing
Replace all private investment with public investment
Cut the cost of production and raise the speed of doing business
Maximise taxation and reduce industrial employment
accepted.x: The policy motto is to cut the cost of production and raise the speed of doing business.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact wording of the policy motto and avoid opposite-policy distractors.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Auto — Sustenance sector
2. Aerospace — Propelling sector
3. Textiles — Propelling sector
4. Blue economy — Propelling sector
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Auto is a Sustenance sector, while aerospace and blue economy are Propelling sectors. Textiles is a Sustenance sector, not a Propelling sector.
accepted.tq: Use the sector classification to detect the swapped category.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: In the investment classification under Industrial Development Policy (4.0), a Mega unit generally falls in which investment band, with land excluded?
accepted.x: A Mega unit falls in the ₹1,000 crore to ₹5,000 crore investment band, with land excluded.
accepted.tq: Match the unit category with its investment range.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes an Ultra Mega unit under Industrial Development Policy (4.0)?
o: Investment above ₹5,000 crore, with a tailor-made package and a standard period of four years
Investment below ₹500 crore, with a standard period of two years
Investment between ₹500 crore and ₹1,000 crore, with a fixed 6% subsidy
Investment between ₹1,000 crore and ₹5,000 crore, with a fixed 12% subsidy
accepted.x: Ultra Mega units involve investment above ₹5,000 crore and receive a tailor-made package; the standard period is four years.
accepted.tq: Combine the size threshold with the applicable incentive structure.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: With reference to the investment subsidy for Sub-Large projects, which of the following is correct?
o: 6% of FCI, with no additional support
15% of FCI only for foreign investors
30% of FCI for every Sub-Large project
12% of FCI, with an additional 5% for specified investor categories
accepted.x: The standard investment subsidy for Sub-Large projects is 12% of Fixed Capital Investment, with an additional 5% for women, SC, ST, BC and specially-abled investors.
accepted.tq: Match the project category with the base subsidy and eligible enhancement.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding investment subsidies:
1. Large projects may receive up to 12% investment subsidy.
2. Mega projects may receive up to 15% investment subsidy.
3. The additional 5% benefit is available to women, BC, SC, ST and specially-abled investors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Large projects may receive up to 12%, Mega projects up to 15%, and the specified investor categories are eligible for an additional 5% benefit.
accepted.tq: Check each subsidy rate and the beneficiary-category enhancement separately.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: A Large project under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) has installed only 50% of its capacity. Which investment subsidy condition applies?
o: The project receives no subsidy under any circumstance
The project receives 30% under the Early Bird scheme
accepted.x: For a Large project, the subsidy is limited to 6% when only 50% of capacity is installed; otherwise, the applicable ceiling may be up to 12%.
accepted.tq: Apply the capacity condition rather than relying only on the general category rate.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a standard incentive available across categories under Industrial Development Policy (4.0)?
o: 100% reimbursement of stamp and transfer duty on land purchase or lease
15% capital subsidy on foreign capital investment
Decarbonisation subsidy up to 6% of FCI
accepted.x: A 15% capital subsidy on foreign capital investment is not a standard incentive. Standard incentives include decarbonisation support, stamp and transfer duty reimbursement and land-conversion fee reimbursement.
accepted.tq: Find the foreign-investment claim that is not part of the standard incentive list.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations represents standard incentives applicable under Industrial Development Policy (4.0)?
o: Revival support for sick units, land-duty reimbursement and decarbonisation subsidy
Only foreign capital subsidy and import-duty exemption
A uniform 15% subsidy for all categories and free electricity for five years
Only export turnover subsidy without land-related reimbursement
accepted.x: Standard incentives include revival support for sick units, 100% stamp and transfer duty reimbursement, 100% land-conversion fee reimbursement and decarbonisation subsidy up to 6% of FCI.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing only incentives expressly included in the standard package.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: Under Industrial Development Policy (4.0), 100% net SGST reimbursement is available for:
accepted.x: The policy provides 100% net SGST reimbursement for five years.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact duration attached to the SGST reimbursement.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the power incentive under the policy package?
o: Power at ₹2 per unit for two years
Power at ₹1 per unit for two years
Power at ₹1 per unit for five years
accepted.x: The policy provides power at ₹1 per unit for two years.
accepted.tq: Match the concessional tariff with its precise duration.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: The Employment Creation Subsidy under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) is available up to:
accepted.x: The Employment Creation Subsidy is available up to 10% of Fixed Capital Investment.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the employment-linked subsidy ceiling from the decarbonisation ceiling.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: A local procurement subsidy under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) is linked to:
o: 1% of export turnover for three years
10% of export turnover for two years
5% of domestic turnover for three years
accepted.x: The local procurement subsidy is 1% of export turnover for three years.
accepted.tq: Match the subsidy percentage with its correct base and period.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: The PLI top-up under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) is:
o: 10% of the Government of India PLI incentive, capped at 5% of FCI
5% of the Government of India PLI incentive, capped at 10% of FCI
15% of export turnover, capped at 5% of FCI
accepted.x: The PLI top-up is 10% of the Government of India incentive and is capped at 5% of FCI.
accepted.tq: Keep the subsidy base separate from its maximum cap.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: The Early Bird scheme provides a 30% investment subsidy to the first 200 projects that obtain Consent for Establishment within:
accepted.x: The first 200 projects obtaining Consent for Establishment within 18 months are eligible for a 30% investment subsidy.
accepted.tq: Link the project-count condition with the correct time limit.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: Under the Early Bird scheme, PLI-sector projects obtaining Consent for Establishment within 24 months are eligible for:
accepted.x: PLI-sector projects obtaining Consent for Establishment within 24 months are eligible for a 40% investment subsidy.
accepted.tq: Separate the special PLI-sector rate from the general Early Bird rate.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the policy suite notified on 26 October 2024:
1. Industrial Development Policy (4.0) was issued as G.O.Ms.68.
2. MSME and Entrepreneur Development Policy was issued as G.O.69.
3. Electronics Manufacturing Policy was issued as G.O.70.
4. Food Processing Policy was issued as G.O.71.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The four policy and Government Order pairings are IDP (4.0)—G.O.Ms.68, MSME—G.O.69, Electronics Manufacturing—G.O.70 and Food Processing—G.O.71.
accepted.tq: Verify each Government Order pairing instead of relying on the policy names alone.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with the policy suite notified on 26 October 2024?
o: Private Industrial Parks—Plug and Play; Sustainable Electric Mobility—CDI/APP
Textile and Garments—G.O.Ms.68; IT and GCC—G.O.70
accepted.x: The suite included Private Industrial Parks, described as Plug and Play, and Sustainable Electric Mobility, associated with CDI/APP.
accepted.tq: Use the policy-description pairing to eliminate swapped Government Orders and companion policies.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: The Textile and Garments Policy 2024-29 and the IT and GCC Policy (4.0) became effective on:
accepted.x: The companion Textile and Garments Policy 2024-29 and IT and GCC Policy (4.0) became effective on 12 December 2024.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the effective date of companion policies from the notification date of the main policy suite.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: In the context of Industrial Development Policy (4.0), FCI stands for:
accepted.x: FCI means Fixed Capital Investment.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar-looking financial abbreviations by identifying the exact official term.
accepted.sec: AP Industrial Development Policy editions - period, thrust areas, standard incentives

accepted.s: A policy provides 12% of FCI as an investment subsidy and an additional 5% for women, BC, SC, ST and specially-abled investors. The additional benefit is best understood as:
o: A replacement for the basic subsidy
A reimbursement limited to land-conversion charges
A subsidy calculated only on export turnover
An enhancement over the basic subsidy for specified investor categories
accepted.x: The additional 5% is an enhancement available to specified investor categories over the applicable basic investment subsidy.
accepted.tq: Apply the distinction between a base incentive and an additional category-based benefit.
